existing_roles.title: Director, United States Operations Quality Audits & Inspections
existing_roles.description:
Facility: Quality

Location:
Plainsboro, NJ, US

**About the Department**

  

The Clinical, Medical and Regulatory (CMR) department at Novo Nordisk is one of the most diverse and collaborative groups within the organization. From healthcare provider interactions and developing and implementing regulatory strategies with the FDA to providing medical education and collecting data to support efficacy and new product development, CMR is involved. The one thing that keeps us all marching to the same beat is our patient centered focus. At Novo Nordisk, you will help patients around the world. As their needs evolve, so does our challenge to find better and more innovative ways to improve their quality of life. We’re changing lives for a living. Are you ready to make a difference?

  

**The Position**

Lead independent, risk-based quality audits and inspection readiness across the approved USO Quality (USOQ) domain. Develop and execute the audit and self-inspection strategy to assess compliance, control effectiveness and risks to patient safety, product quality and data integrity across applicable current GxPs [Good Clinical (GCP), Pharmacovigilance (GPV), Distribution (GDP) and Manufacturing (GMP)] practices]. Maintain an objective view of business and Quality activities, including outsourced activities within scope. Lead sustained audit and inspection readiness and act as the designated local health authority inspection point of contact and inspection lead for the USOQ domain, coordinating with Regulatory Affairs, Global Quality, Patient Safety and accountable business leaders. Ensure readiness gaps and regulatory commitments are visible, owned, and escalated. Provide independent assurance over external-party quality controls through risk-based audits & remediation plans.

  

**Relationships**

Position reports to the Head of USO Quality. The sponsor approves the audit charter and risk-based plan, reviews resource adequacy, receives unfiltered findings and has formal input into the Director’s appointment, removal and performance assessment. The Director has direct access to the sponsor to escalate interference, disputed findings, scope restrictions and unresolved material risks. Interface with multiple Novo accountable business leaders, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, Safety, global Quality Audit and Global Clinical Compliance. External relationships include health authorities, clinical trial sites, external auditors and relevant vendors and partners. Coordinate USOQ inspection communications through approved authority channels without displacing global, legal-entity, Regulatory or Safety accountabilities. This role manages the independent audit and inspection department, with multiple experienced quality representatives assigned to diverse quality functions and includes auditor competence, inspection leadership, workload, budget and continuity.

  

**Essential Functions**

* Direct Independent Audits and Self-Inspection Program & Staff
* Maintain the USOQ audit charter, audit universe and risk-based audit and self-inspection strategy. Define scope, frequency, methods, auditor qualifications and escalation criteria across business functions, Quality verticals and relevant external parties. Secure approval of audit plans and material changes, ensure authorized access to personnel, sites, systems and records and align with global audit programs to prevent duplication and coverage gaps
* Lead the annual audit & self-inspection program, including routine, risk-triggered and for-cause reviews. Assign qualified, independent auditors; oversee evidence-based assessments of control design, effectiveness, data integrity and external-party controls. Ensure consistent finding classification, clear communication and timely reporting. Manage budget and staffing, document plan deviations and escalate material coverage or resource gaps
* Inspection Readiness and Health Authority Leadership
* Lead inspection readiness with business and Quality leaders through assessments, mock inspections, playbooks, document-retrieval exercises, SME preparation and trained deputies. Define inspection-team roles, front- and back-room responsibilities, request tracking and escalation. Coordinate USOQ administrative support while leading readiness coordination and independent challenge. Business and process owners retain responsibility for compliant operations, source records and readiness evidence
* Serve as the designated local health authority inspection contact and lead within approved USOQ scope, including FDA and other formally assigned authorities. Coordinate inspection logistics, meetings, interviews, requests and communications with Regulatory Affairs, global functions and accountable SMEs. Lead observation triage, response coordination and commitment tracking. Secure authorized approvals for submissions, commitments and risk acceptance; retain established company signatory, Regulatory and Safety reporting authorities
* Finding Ownership and Remediation Oversight
* Ensure all audit, self-inspection and inspection findings have accountable business or process owners, action owners, deadlines and escalation routes. Business leaders assign ownership and resources; finding owners investigate root causes, develop and implement CAPA and demonstrate effectiveness. Quality owns findings within its processes. Challenge inadequate responses and escalate unassigned, overdue, repeat or high-risk findings to the Head of USOQ and Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor, as appropriate. Honor health authority deadlines
* Independently assess audit and self-inspection responses and verify remediation effectiveness before closing findings under approved procedures. Require additional evidence or action where needed. For inspection observations, coordinate completion and effectiveness checks while preserving authorized response approvals and health authority closure decisions. Reviewers must not assess their own remediation; finding owners retain investigation, CAPA development and implementation
* Report audit themes, inspection readiness, overdue commitments and systemic risks to the Quality Council and relevant global forums. Escalate urgent risks immediately and independence concerns directly to the Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor
* Independence and Performance
* Protect audit objectivity through a documented charter, conflict disclosures, independent assignments and unfiltered reporting. Base conclusions on evidence, free from business or delivery pressures; escalate classification disputes through approved independent channels. Do not operate or approve controls the team audits; arrange independent review of its readiness and inspection-coordination activities. Track risk-based coverage, reporting and regulatory-response timeliness, readiness-gap closure, overdue and repeat findings, CAPA effectiveness and auditor competence. Do not incentivize low finding counts or guarantee inspection outcomes.
  

**Physical Requirements**

10-20% overnight travel required. This position (in-office) is located in Plainsboro, NJ.

  

**Development Of People**

Supervisory. Ensure that reporting personnel have individual development plans (IDP), with annual goals and measurements that are consistent with the priorities of the business and that interim reviews are held so that their work is focused on those priorities and they understand their level of accountability for results and the measurement process. Ensure that the IDP forms include completed learning and aspiration plans and are in place for all reporting personnel to enable the achievement of goals and capability to assume increased levels of responsibility. Manage the application and communication of all Novo Nordisk policies, procedures and Novo Nordisk Way.

  

**Qualifications**

* **Education level:** Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree preferred; advanced degree may substitute for 2 years of experience
* **Experience Level:** 10+ years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry, including at least 5 years in GxP Quality Assurance, Compliance, or related functions, and 5 years in people leadership or leading complex cross-functional quality initiatives. Demonstrated experience in commercial/affiliate quality, pharmacovigilance quality, regulatory inspections, and pharmaceutical Quality Management Systems (QMS). Broader GDP/GMP experience preferred.
* **Specific or technical job skills:** Deep expertise in GxP and FDA inspections; working knowledge of GPV/GDP/GMP/GCP and other requirements applicable to commercial & post-marketing operations. Job Description
  
  
Position Overview
  
  
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
  
Global Quality Management Systems
  
  
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
  
  
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
  
  
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
  
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
  
  

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
  
  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
  
  

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:**  
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
  
  
**Preferred Skills:**  
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

ADC Therapeutics (NYSE): is a commercial, global leader and pioneer in the field of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) with specialized capabilities from clinical through commercialization. ZYNLONTA is also being evaluated in combination with other agents and in earlier lines of DLBCL therapy as well as indolent lymphomas including follicular lymphoma and marginal zone lymphoma with the potential to reach significantly more patients through expanded use.

We are a team of approximately 150 patient-focused, purpose-driven employees with a shared mission to transform the treatment paradigm for patients. If you’re interested in making a difference in the lives of patients worldwide with a team of like-minded colleagues, operating in a flexible work environment, come join us on our journey! To learn more about ADC Therapeutics, our values, and our exceptional culture, please visit us at https://adctherapeutics.com/ and LinkedIn.

**Job Summary****:**

The Senior Director of Manufacturing Sciences & Technologies (MSAT) is a senior technical leader responsible for end-to-end process ownership, technical oversight, and lifecycle management of drug substance intermediates, ADC drug substance, and ADC drug product manufactured through a global network of external CDMOs.

This role ensures robust, scalable, and compliant manufacturing processes that support commercial manufacturing, process development projects and clinical development, while serving as the senior-level technical support for internal Production Management Teams and external manufacturing partners.

The position plays a critical role in process validation, technology transfer, continued process verification (CPV), change management, technical and regulatory support across antibody, linker-payload, conjugation, formulation, fill/finish, and packaging operations.

This position reports to the Vice President, Global Supply & Operations. The role is remote based, with a preference for candidates located on the U.S. East Coast.

**What You'll Do****:**

MSAT Strategy and Leadership

* Lead and develop the MSAT function covering ADC end-to-end manufacturing across clinical and commercial stages.
* Define MSAT strategy for external manufacturing aligned with corporate objectives.
* Develop and mentor a high-performing MSAT team with deep expertise in biologics, highly potent payloads, and aseptic operations.
* Serve as a key member of the Operations Management Team to contribute to long-term supply, risk mitigation, and operational excellence initiatives.

Manufacturing Process Oversight (External Manufacturing)

* Accountable for overall manufacturing process stewardship, ensure robust process knowledge management and align process understanding within ADCT and at the CDMO partners.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to ensure ADCT’s Production Management Teams effectively interface and manage CDMO performance.
* Oversee and guide: MSAT activities at CDMOs, process characterization, validation (PPQ), process monitoring and CPV programs.
* Ensure consistent process understanding and control across global manufacturing partners.
* Drive effective issue resolution for manufacturing deviations, CAPAs, and change requests.
* Support CDMO selection, technical due diligence, and onboarding for new manufacturing partners.

Process Lifecycle Management

* Provide scientific and technical oversight across the full ADC manufacturing lifecycle.
* Assess and implement post approval changes, comparability strategies, and process optimization initiatives.
* Oversee and endorse process improvements to enhance process robustness, yield, cost, and supply reliability.

Regulatory & Quality Support

* Serve as the senior-level accountable MSAT person for regulatory submissions and inspections, including INDs, BLAs, MAAs, supplements to these filings.
* Author, review, and approve CMC regulatory sections and responses.
* Support health authority inspections and technical audits of CDMOs.
* Partner closely with Quality to ensure compliance with cGMP, ICH, and global regulatory expectations.
* Ensure sound scientific justifications for process control strategies, specifications, and lifecycle changes.

Cross Functional Collaboration

* Collaborate closely with Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Supply Chain and CMC Regulatory
* Provide MSAT input into development programs, commercial readiness, and long range supply planning.
* Participate in internal governance forums, change control boards, and technical review committees.

Risk Management & Continuous Improvement

* Establish and track critical process parameters (CPPs) and CPV metrics.
* Proactively identify and mitigate technical and operational risks within ADC Therapeutics’ external manufacturing network.
* Drive lessons learned, standardization, and continuous improvement across CDMOs and Production Management Teams.

Requirements:

**Who You Are****:**

* Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, or related field; BS with significant industry experience considered.
* 12+ years of relevant experience including biologics manufacturing, CMC operations, and CDMO management.
* Extensive experience in commercial GMP manufacturing operations, process validation, CPV, and regulatory submission preparation.
* Strong scientific problem-solving and root-cause analysis skills.
* Proven ability to lead through influence in external or remote environments.
* Excellent communication skills for executive, regulatory, and partner interfaces
* Strategic thinker with strong execution focus.
* Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, commercial-stage organization.
* Deep knowledge of relevant bioconjugate technologies is preferred (antibody, high potency linker-payload, conjugation, aseptic fill and lyophilization).
* Strong track record of building and leading technical and cross-functional teams.
* Visionary leadership with a strategic mindset.
* High standards of excellence, urgency, and accountability.
* Collaborative, team-oriented approach.
* Strong organizational and critical thinking skills.
* Ability to mentor, influence, and drive change across a remote organization.
* Domestic and international travel up to 20%, primarily to CDMOs.

**What We Offer****:**

* Competitive biotech base salary, annual target bonus (eligibility based on company performance) or quarterly IC (field sales roles) and new hire stock options – so you share in the value you help create
* Medical, Dental and Vision benefits which start on the 1st day of employment
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off and company holidays including a company wide shut down at the end of the year
* Paid Parental Leave, Life and Disability Insurance, Tax advantaged health savings and spending accounts
* A hands-on, collaborative culture with other passionate biotech professionals
* Mission-driven work that puts patients first

**Join Our Inclusive Team****:**

ADC Therapeutics is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building collaborative, engaged teams and fostering a professional and respectful work environment where employees are empowered for success. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by law.

Position Summary

The Director, Digital Twin & Intelligent Manufacturing Capabilities is responsible for defining and advancing the enterprise strategy, technology direction, governance, standards, and capability roadmap for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, Automation-enabled Manufacturing, and AI-driven manufacturing capabilities across Global Technical Operations (GTO). This role serves as GTO's enterprise leader for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities and is accountable for shaping how manufacturing science, process knowledge, automation, data, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and digital technologies are leveraged to improve technology transfer, process understanding, manufacturing readiness, operational performance, and business outcomes across the product lifecycle.

The Director will partner closely with MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Singapore manufacturing and digital organizations, Alexion, FMC, Regional Digital Leads, Manufacturing, IT, Enterprise Architecture, Data & AI, Automation, and Site Digital teams to establish enterprise-scale capabilities and implementation frameworks that can be deployed consistently across the manufacturing network. While Regional Digital Leads and site organizations retain accountability for site-level deployment and adoption, this role is responsible for defining the enterprise capability strategy, technology direction, operating model, governance, standards, and reusable assets required to scale Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities across GTO.

This position requires deep expertise in Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities, combined with strong technology leadership, manufacturing and process-science credibility, automation awareness, systems thinking, vendor evaluation experience, AI and advanced analytics fluency, and a proven ability to lead large-scale cross-functional transformation initiatives in complex global organizations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Enterprise Strategy & Capability Leadership**

* Define and maintain the enterprise strategy for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities across GTO.

* Establish and evolve a multi-year capability roadmap aligned with GTO priorities, Digital Tech Transfer strategy, manufacturing modernization initiatives, and enterprise digital objectives.

* Identify strategic opportunities to improve technology transfer, process characterization, scale-up, manufacturing readiness, process robustness, operational performance, and business value.

* Develop capability maturity models, adoption frameworks, and value realization approaches to support enterprise scaling.

* Translate business needs and manufacturing challenges into actionable capability roadmaps, standards, investment priorities, and implementation approaches.

**Technology, Automation & Intelligent Manufacturing Leadership**

* Assess emerging technologies and industry developments to guide future capability investments and roadmap decisions.

* Establish approaches for connecting process knowledge, manufacturing systems, automation platforms, process data, simulations, and Digital Twins through effective data flows and information architectures.

* Guide build-versus-buy decisions and strategic technology direction for Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities.

**Process Intelligence, Modeling & Digital Twin Governance**

* Establish governance frameworks, standards, methodologies, and best practices for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities across GTO.

* Define and oversee model lifecycle management approaches, including model transition, deployment, maintenance, monitoring, documentation, and retirement.

* Establish ownership models, stewardship expectations, support models, and decision-making frameworks for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities.

* Develop reusable methods, templates, and standards that enable scalability and consistency across products, sites, and manufacturing networks.

* Ensure Digital Twin and Process Intelligence initiatives are aligned to enterprise quality, regulatory, and operational expectations.

**Community of Practice & Capability Development**

* Build and maintain a network of practitioners and subject matter experts across Manufacturing, MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Automation, IT, Data & AI, Site Digital organizations, and Regional Digital Leads.

* Develop standards, reference architectures, implementation guidance, training materials, and best practices to support capability maturity and enterprise adoption.

* Promote innovation, knowledge sharing, and capability development across the organization.

* Sponsor and oversee Digital Twin and Process Intelligence initiatives involving interns, graduate students, and university partnerships aligned to strategic business priorities.

* Collaborate with academic institutions, innovation partners, and external research organizations to advance Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities.

**Enterprise Transformation & Business Partnership**

* Partner closely with MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Singapore manufacturing organizations, Alexion, FMC, and Manufacturing organizations to identify opportunities and shape future-state capabilities.

* Ensure Digital Twin and Process Intelligence strategies align with broader Digital Tech Transfer, Intelligent Manufacturing, and GTO transformation objectives.

* Lead complex cross-functional initiatives requiring alignment across business, scientific, manufacturing, digital, and technology organizations.

* Influence strategic decisions and drive organizational alignment without direct authority.

* Translate emerging technologies into scalable business capabilities and measurable outcomes.

**External Innovation & Vendor Management**

* Build and manage relationships with strategic technology vendors, industry organizations, academic partners, and innovation ecosystems.

* Lead technology assessments, proof-of-concept initiatives, capability evaluations, and vendor-selection activities.

* Monitor industry developments in Digital Twins, Process Intelligence, Manufacturing Analytics, Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Intelligent Manufacturing.

* Guide strategic partnerships and investment decisions that strengthen GTO’s long-term Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities.

**Qualifications**

Required

**Preferred**

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin**  
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

  

As a Sr. Director for Manufacturing at Blue Origin’s manufacturing, production, and launch facilities, this role will have a direct impact on the success of Blue’s mission.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.

  

**About This Opportunity**  
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking an experienced Sr. Director with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of our rocket production program. This role will span the following functional areas:

Manufacturing and Integration
  
Provides senior leadership across production operations including structural fabrication, thermal protection systems, systems integration, testing, and final assembly for Blue Origin’s booster manufacturing. Responsible for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle. This role will also provide leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:**  
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
  

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

  
**Minimum Qualifications:**  

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30

You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Description:

**Lead Strategy. Drive Performance. Shape the Future.**

KSP Group, Inc/Jensen Metal Products is seeking a hands-on manufacturing leader to drive operational excellence, strengthen accountability, improve execution, and build scalable operating systems across our manufacturing businesses. This is not a corporate executive role designed to lead from a conference room.

We are looking for a proven change agent who is equally comfortable reviewing financial results, leading daily operational reviews, solving production challenges on the shop floor, and developing frontline leaders.

This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.

**About KSP Group**

KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies

* **Jensen Metal Products** – Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
* **Jensen Powder Finishers** – Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI)
* **Jensen Castings** – Manufacturer of premium GFRC concrete fire features (Richland Center, WI)
* **Real Flame** – A leading designer and manufacturer of fireplaces, fire tables, and outdoor living products sold through major retailers across North America (Union Grove, WI)

Together, our companies are built on innovation, craftsmanship, customer partnerships, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a visible impact, influence company strategy, and help shape the future of multiple growing businesses.

**What You'll Do**

Executive Strategic & Business Leadership

* Lead the development and execution of operational strategies that support long-term business objectives and growth initiatives
* Partner with executive leadership to establish priorities, allocate resources, and drive enterprise-wide operational improvements
* Lead plant leadership teams in defining strategic direction, performance goals, and key operational initiatives
* Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, capacity expansion, and operational scalability

Financial & Operational Performance

* Own operational performance and P&L results across assigned manufacturing operations
* Develop departmental budgets, monitor spending, and ensure responsible management of operational resources
* Analyze manufacturing costs, labor efficiency, productivity metrics, and operating expenses to drive profitability
* Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership

Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives across fabrication, welding, machining, powder coating, assembly, engineering, and support functions
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, root cause problem solving, and waste reduction efforts
* Improve throughput, quality, safety, delivery performance, and overall operational efficiency
* Lead cross-functional projects focused on sustainable operational gains and measurable business results

Leadership & Culture

* Build, coach, and develop high-performing operational leadership teams
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement
* Promote employee engagement while creating a safe, quality-focused work environment

Requirements:

**What We're Looking For**

* Demonstrated success leading directly from the manufacturing floor, including personal involvement in:
* Production planning and scheduling
* Labor performance management
* Quality improvement initiatives
* Corrective action processes
* Maintenance and equipment planning
* Capital investment justification
* Safety and operational accountability
* Frontline leadership development
* Proven track record of transforming entrepreneurial manufacturing organizations into process-driven, scalable operations through both strategic leadership and active engagement with frontline teams
* Ability to establish accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy
* Strong understanding of fabrication, welding, machining, finishing, assembly, materials management, and manufacturing cost drivers

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or related field, preferred
* Multi-site manufacturing leadership experience
* Lean Six Sigma certification
* Experience within both contract manufacturing and consumer products environments
* ERP/MRP system experience

**Travel Requirements**

* Regular travel between KSP Group facilities, including Jensen Metal Products, Jensen Powder Finishers, Jensen Castings, and Real Flame locations
* Frequent presence on manufacturing floors to support leadership teams, operational reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Approximately 25-50% travel, primarily within Wisconsin and company operating locations
* Occasional overnight travel for customer visits, supplier meetings, strategic initiatives, and industry events

**About Us**

Jensen Metal Products is a metal fabrication business with over 100 years of experience serving the Midwest and surrounding regions with custom, quality sheet metal parts and assemblies. With a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, we produce a diverse portfolio of products, including our own line of fireplaces, which has been in production since 1970. We serve many types of businesses including the agricultural, retail, energy and healthcare fields. From engineering to packaging, our goal is to be a one-stop shop that exceeds our customers’ expectations for quality, delivery, great customer service and cost. At Jensen Metal Products we pride ourselves on having strong, long-lasting relationships with our employees and customers. We welcome you to join our team!

**Benefits**

* Competitive base salary plus profit sharing
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options (HDHP and copay), FSA benefits, and the ability to use your existing HSA
* Company-funded medical deductible reimbursement — up to $1,000 (individual) / $2,000 (family)
* 401(k) with company match up to 4%
* Life and disability insurance and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Paid time off and company holidays
* Annual Safety PPE Reimbursement
* A collaborative, team-oriented environment with direct access to leadership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a growing organization
* Company-sponsored team events and outings that foster connection and celebrate team success

**Work Authorization**

Jensen Metal Products does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

**Recruiting Agencies**

Jensen Metal Products does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies, recruiting firms, or search agencies. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to Jensen Metal Products employees or through our application process will become the property of Jensen Metal Products, and no fee will be paid if the candidate is hired.

existing_roles.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
  
  
Company Overview
  
At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.
  
  
Position Brand Description
  
How would you like a career where you get to apply your best technical and analytical skills to bring complex, high-potency biologic medicines to patients? We are seeking a scientific leader on our Parenteral Product Network Technical Services/Manufacturing Science (TS/MS) team to drive the commercialization of lyophilized drug products, with a focus on antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), and to provide technical support for commercial lyophilized product manufacturing.
  
In this role, you are critical to the success of Lilly’s oncology and biologics portfolio. As a Global Product Steward and lyophilization process expert, you will hold technical ownership of assigned lyophilized ADC and other parenteral products from late-stage development through the commercial lifecycle, serving as the technical link between Product Development and our commercial manufacturing sites. You will ensure these products are successfully launched, reliably supplied, and technically well controlled across internal and external sites.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
As an individual contributor, you will work side by side with colleagues in Product Development, Manufacturing Operations, Quality, EHS, and Supply Chain, as well as with external manufacturing organizations. You will be a visible technical presence in cross-functional teams, mentor junior technical associates, and escalate significant technical, quality, safety, and supply risks to management with clear assessments and recommended actions.
  
  
**Key responsibilities include:**  

* Serve as Global Product Steward and subject matter expert for lyophilized, ADC and parenteral products, holding end-to-end technical accountability for process performance, product quality, and supply across all manufacturing sites, and serving as the primary technical interface between Product Development and commercial manufacturing.
* Advance lyophilization technology in commercial manufacturing
* Maintain the product technical knowledge base and lifecycle strategy, including process history, critical material and supplier knowledge, a product technical risk register, and a roadmap for yield, robustness, capacity, and site-network improvements.
* Collaborate with product development and manufacturing site for technology transfer, scale-up, process performance qualification/validation, and comparability activities (including lyophilization cycle transfer between freeze-dryers of differing scale and design) to support commercial launch readiness.
* Escalate significant technical, quality, safety, compliance, and supply risks to TS/MS management in a timely manner, providing risk assessments, impact to patients and supply, and recommended mitigation plans.
* Own the commercial control strategy for lyophilization critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, and maintain process understanding through continued process verification, stability and batch trending, and global product assessment.
* Partner with Product Development to ensure manufacturability of new ADC and lyophilized products, and to provide commercial manufacturing feedback that informs formulation, cycle design, specifications, container closure selection, and site selection.
* Author and review technical sections of global regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and responses to regulatory questions, and support inspection readiness at commercial sites.
* Lead process improvement and lifecycle management projects, including introduction of new lyophilization, filling, and containment technologies and qualification of vials, stoppers, and other critical materials.

Basic Qualifications
  
  

* A degree in a relevant area such as Pharmaceutical Science, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, or Chemistry with one of the following:
* PhD degree with 5 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Master’s degree with 10 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Bachelor’s degree with 15 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing.
* Hands-on experience with lyophilization development or manufacturing (e.g., formulation and cycle development, scale-up, tech transfer, or commercial cycle support).
* Working knowledge of protein-based and ADC drug product formulation and aseptic fill/finish processes.
* Experience supporting GMP commercial manufacturing, including technology transfer, process validation, and/or deviation investigation and resolution.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B or TN status) for this employment position.
  
  
Additional Skills/Preferences
  
We want you to bring your lyophilization and biologics expertise, commercial manufacturing experience, and technical influence to help launch and supply ADC and other lyophilized medicines.
  
  
**Preferred experience includes:**  

* Direct ADC drug product experience, including handling of cytotoxic or highly potent payloads and the stability and process sensitivities of conjugated antibodies.
* Background in lyophilized product development, including formulation and excipient selection, freeze-drying cycle design, and thermal characterization, and cycle scale-up.
* Analytical characterization of lyophilized biologics and ADCs
* Experience with container closure and critical material qualification, including vial and stopper selection, container closure integrity, and the interaction of materials with processing equipment.
* Product stewardship experience, such as serving as technical owner or product lead for a commercial or late-stage product, authoring annual product reviews or technical risk assessments, and managing multi-site process harmonization.
* Demonstrated leadership, influence, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret complex technical data, troubleshoot manufacturing issues, and clearly escalate risks and recommendations to management.
* Preparation, review, and response to global regulatory submissions (e.g., BLAs, NDAs, or equivalent), post-approval changes, and support of regulatory inspections.
* Working knowledge of statistical design of experiments and analysis, and of containment strategies and occupational exposure limits for potent compounds.
* Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across Development, Operations, Quality, EHS, and external manufacturing partners.

We’re also excited if you bring an insatiable desire to learn, to innovate, and to challenge yourself for the benefit of patients.
  
  
Additional Information
  
  

* Recognition and future promotion on the Technical Ladder
* 10–20% domestic and international travel to commercial manufacturing sites and partners (to be confirmed by leadership)
* Lilly is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

Lilly is dedicated to helping individuals with disabilities to actively engage in the workforce, ensuring equal opportunities when vying for positions. If you require accommodation to submit a resume for a position at Lilly, please complete the accommodation request form (https://careers.lilly.com/us/en/workplace-accommodation) for further assistance. Please note this is for individuals to request an accommodation as part of the application process and any other correspondence will not receive a response.
  
  
Lilly is proud to be an EEO Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, ancestry, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.
  
  
Our employee resource groups (ERGs) offer strong support networks for their members and are open to all employees. Our current groups include: Africa, Middle East, Central Asia (AMECA), Black Employees at Lilly (BE@Lilly), Chinese Culture Network (CCN), EnAble, Evolve, Lilly Indian Network (LIN), Organization of Latinx at Lilly (OLA), Pride (LGBTQ+ Allies), Veterans Leadership Network (VLN) and Women’s Initiative for Leading at Lilly (WILL).
  
  
Actual compensation will depend on a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. The anticipated wage for this position is
  
$130,500 - $211,200
  
  
Full-time equivalent employees also will be eligible for a company bonus (depending, in part, on company and individual performance). In addition, Lilly offers a comprehensive benefit program to eligible employees, including eligibility to participate in a company-sponsored 401(k); pension; vacation benefits; eligibility for medical, dental, vision and prescription drug benefits; flexible benefits (e.g., healthcare and/or dependent day care flexible spending accounts); life insurance and death benefits; certain time off and leave of absence benefits; and well-being benefits (e.g., employee assistance program, fitness benefits, and employee clubs and activities).Lilly reserves the right to amend, modify, or terminate its compensation and benefit programs in its sole discretion and Lilly’s compensation practices and guidelines will apply regarding the details of any promotion or transfer of Lilly employees.

**Purpose**
  
Under minimal supervisor, manages the daily, on-going production operations of an assigned plant(s). Oversees plant personnel providing guidance and direction to lower level management. Drives customer focused business strategy through maintaining optimal plant operation and accurate inventory management.
  
  
**Focus & Scope**
  
*Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:*

* Oversees the daily aggregate mining, processing and asphalt operations at an assigned plant(s).

* Manages assigned staff to include: hiring, training, and development. Determines workflow and staff priorities.

* Conducts business in a professional, legal and environmentally sound manner in adherence to company policies.

* Analyzes financial and operational plant performance including operating margin, cost, key production indicators, and inventory management.

* Administers short and long range plant planning, coordinates production schedules and costs, as well as plant flow evaluation, maintenance and inventory control.

* Ensures that plants are in good operating condition at all times and proposes changes and modifications as required. Maximizes efficiencies through systems and automation.

* Collaborates with the Engineering Department to develop capital expenditure analysis for plant improvements.

* Confers with sales personnel in preparation of annual sales budgets.

* Determines annual plant operating budget and manages to budget.

* Monitors union contracts for workforce and company compliance. May participate in union/company contract negotiations.

* Develops a Zero Injury culture by setting expectations, coaching behavior, and adhering to all company safety policies and practices.

  
**Qualifications, Requirements, & Competencies**
  
  
Education

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Construction Management or Business or an equivalent combination of training, education and experience.

  
Experience & Industry Expertise:

* A minimum of five (5) years of experience in an aggregate or asphalt environment or an equivalent combination of training and related experience. An advanced understanding of Aggregate plant operations and products.

  
Specific Job Requirements:

* Three (3) years experience managing staff.
* Must demonstrate ability to effectively lead, manage, coach, mentor and develop staff.
* Must demonstrate ability to formulate and implement new or improved processes, procedures or tactics.
* Must demonstrate ability to work in a fast-paced environment, prioritize and manage multiple assignments.
* Must demonstrate the ability to originate and drive operation initiatives, changes and enhancements.
* Must develop and maintain strong working relationships internally and externally with diverse groups of people.
* Must possess excellent verbal and written communications skills with the ability to speak, write and understand English at a proficient and understandable level.
* Must demonstrate the ability work well under pressure, remaining composed and professional. Must demonstrate strong organizational skills and time management practices.

Competencies

* Building Successful Teams

* Communication
* Judgment/Decision-Making
* Managing Complexity

**Seating Plant Manager**

**Position Summary**
====================

DARRAN is a family-owned furniture manufacturer based in High Point, North Carolina, creating thoughtfully designed furniture for 50 years. Our work brings together craftsmanship, innovation, and a commitment to quality, supported by people who take pride in what they build.
===================================================================================================================================================================================================================================================================================

We are seeking a Production Manager over our Seating Operations to guide our seating manufacturing operation and support its continued growth. This leadership role brings together people, processes, and craftsmanship to build a strong team and deliver exceptional products. The ideal candidate leads by example, develops others, and creates an environment where accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement are part of everyday work.


**Management and People Leadership**
====================================

* Direct and supervise seating department employees, assign work, communicate daily priorities, and hold employees accountable for meeting expectations.
* Set clear expectations for productivity, quality, attendance, conduct, and safe work practices. Ensure employees understand their responsibilities and department goals.
* Monitor individual and team performance daily, including output, work quality, efficiency, attendance, and adherence to established procedures. Identify concerns and address them promptly.
* Provide ongoing coaching and timely feedback. Establish improvement expectations, document follow-up, and verify that required improvements are achieved and sustained.
* Administer and document disciplinary actions in partnership with HR and in accordance with company policy. Clearly communicate the concern, required correction, and consequences of continued issues.
* Complete annual performance reviews and provide accurate, specific feedback supported by documented performance observations.
* Partner with HR on hiring and employee matters. Coordinate onboarding and training, assess employee skills, and identify development and cross-training needs.
* Apply company policies consistently, address employee concerns respectfully, and maintain clear communication with employees, HR, and senior operations leadership.

**Production**
==============

* Lead daily production startup and ensure teams, materials, and priorities are ready at the beginning of each shift.
* Manage production flow across frame building, cutting, sewing, upholstering, and final assembly to keep work on schedule.
* Partner with senior operations leadership to review daily objectives, constraints, and priorities.
* Drive results across output, delivery performance, labor utilization, overtime, quality, and production flow.
* Develop and improve standard operating procedures and processes that increase throughput and reduce bottlenecks.
* Coordinate with outside and original-equipment suppliers to maintain production capacity and quality standards while expanding internal capabilities.
* Collaborate with engineering and product development on patterns, production readiness, and the launch of new seating collections.
* Establish, maintain, and enforce quality checks and corrective actions.
* Coordinate maintenance needs, execute safety programs, and reinforce safe work practices throughout the operation.
* Advance shop-floor organization and housekeeping practices that support a structured, clean, and efficient workplace.

**How Success Is Measured**
===========================

Success is measured by consistent people leadership and department results against goals established with senior operations leadership. Performance is evaluated through production and quality reports, employee performance records, training progress, and completion of corrective actions.

* People management and accountability: Employees understand their goals and responsibilities. Performance and attendance concerns are addressed promptly, company policies are applied consistently, and coaching and disciplinary actions are documented with HR.
* Performance improvement: Individual and team results are monitored regularly. Employees receive specific feedback, improvement expectations and follow-up dates are documented, and progress is verified. Annual reviews are completed on time.
* Employee development: New employees complete assigned training, demonstrated skills meet job requirements, and cross-training improves coverage across seating operations.
* Production and delivery: Actual output and on-time completion meet established targets. Bottlenecks and schedule delays are identified early, communicated, and addressed.
* Quality: Products meet established standards. Defects, rework, and recurring quality issues are tracked, and corrective actions produce sustained improvement.
* Labor and operational efficiency: Labor utilization and overtime remain within established expectations. Process improvements reduce avoidable downtime and improve production flow.
* Safety and workplace organization: Safe work practices and housekeeping standards are consistently enforced. Hazards and incidents are reported promptly, and assigned corrective actions are completed by their due dates.
* Communication and follow-through: Priorities, staffing concerns, and production risks are communicated promptly to the appropriate partners. Assigned actions and production readiness milestones are completed on time.

**Qualifications**
==================

* 10+ years of upholstery, pattern, and assembly experience and 5+ years of running an upholstery operation.
* High school diploma or GED required.
* Strong reading, writing, math, analysis, comprehension, administrative, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to set clear priorities, manage and hold people accountable, monitor performance, document personnel matters, and collaborate across operations, HR, engineering, product development, and suppliers.
* A practical, continuous-improvement mindset with a strong commitment to safety, quality, delivery, and respectful people leadership.

**Physical Requirements and Work Environment**
==============================================

This is an on-site role in an active manufacturing environment. The position requires excellent vision, hearing/listening, and clear speech; hand and finger dexterity; lifting and carrying up to 50 pounds; pushing and pulling; local driving; color perception; touch/feel; and the ability to move within and between facilities. Work includes frequent face-to-face and verbal interaction with others and may involve dirt or dust, fumes or odors, moving objects, and work at heights.

**Benefits**
============

401(k), dental insurance, health insurance, life insurance, paid time off, retirement plan, and vision insurance.

**Summary**
-----------

**This posting is open to all qualified candidates.**

  
  
  
  
Are you looking for an opportunity to lead a highly trained team of Operations and Maintenance (O&M) staff and be a part of creating the strategic direction for a complex wastewater system? The Wastewater Treatment Division (WTD) in King County (KC) is hiring a leader for the Brightwater Treatment Plant. This position will lead a team of 40 Operations, maintenance and Facilities staff, oversee the planning and processes for facilities maintenance of the Brightwater system, and be an active member of the O&M Leadership team.
  
  
Working for KC WTD provides you with a work-life balance and benefits to support you and your family. You will also gain opportunities for growth through training, conferences hosted by leaders in the industry, and working across functional groups within the Division.
  
  
We are looking for creative and innovative thinking that drives us to continuously improve public service. Tap into your desire to serve the public and discover new and better ways to make a meaningful impact by joining the WTD O&M Leadership team.
  
  
**About the Role:**
  
This is a leadership position and will serve on the Operations and Maintenance Section Leadership team. This team is responsible for the strategic planning of the section, developing leadership skills among our supervisors, providing growth opportunities for our staff, and implementing metrics to deliver key performance measures that contribute to the overall growth and success of WTD Operations and Maintenance.
  
  
In this role, the successful candidate will apply their skillset in the areas of planning, coordination, scope, budget, schedule management, monitoring and control, and reporting in the maintenance and development of the Brightwater Treatment System.
  
  
**About the Team:**
  
The Operations and Maintenance Section of the Wastewater Treatment Division is tasked with ensuring safe, environmentally protective wastewater treatment for King County, serving 34 wholesale customers and approximately 2.3 million residents. The Section includes five treatment facilities, 48 pump stations, 400 miles of conveyance piping and treats an average of 185MGD of wastewater. We are a clean water utility, recovering resources such as biosolids, recycled water and biogas, continually seeking new ways to capture beneficial uses of resources that would otherwise be lost.
  
  
WTD is committed to the principles of equity and social justice (ESJ). We value diverse perspectives and life experiences in our workforce and are committed to building a culturally diverse and inclusive environment. WTD strives to provide equitable services to residents and businesses across King County. Our department vision is to provide sustainable and livable communities and a clean and healthy natural environment that supports a prosperous and resilient economy.  
  
  

Join our team dedicated to ensuring clean water for generations to come! With over 1000 employees engaged in planning, designing, building, and operating treatment facilities, our agency is at the forefront of environmental stewardship. Success for us means upholding our legacy while promising future generations a pristine environment.

  
  

We partner with regulatory agencies to reduce harmful waste discharge and actively educate the public and businesses on water quality protection. We prioritize accountability to our ratepayers and operate a well-managed agency that services over 2.3 million King County residents. Our regional wastewater treatment system not only sustains a healthy environment but also fuels economic development, fostering prosperity in our region. If you're passionate about making a difference and thrive in a collaborative environment, join us in our mission to safeguard our precious water resources.

  
  

**Commitment to Equity, Racial and Social Justice:**

King County, named after Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., is a diverse and vibrant community that represents cultures from around the world. We prioritize equity, racial and social justice, making it a foundational and daily expectation for all employees. As a Wastewater Treatment Plant Manager, you will actively apply these principles in all aspects of your work. Learn more about our commitment at http://www.kingcounty.gov/equity.

  
  

**Apply now for a rewarding career at the** **Wastewater Treatment Division** **of King County Department of Natural Resources & Parks (DNRP). Join our talented workforce in protecting and restoring the natural environment and promoting more resilient, sustainable, and equitable communities. Enjoy training,** **comprehensive benefits****, and growth opportunities.**

**Job Duties**
--------------

**What You Will Be Doing:**

Reporting to the Director of Eden, the Plant Manager is accountable for day-to-day plant performance, including safety, production, quality, financial results, maintenance, continuous improvement and on-time customer delivery.

This is an on-site role based at Eden Millwork in Knox, Pennsylvania.

You will maintain a strong presence on the production floor, build accountability across the team, and partner closely with Metrie leaders and support functions.

**You will**

* Lead day-to-day plant operations, aligning production, scheduling, maintenance, staffing, materials, and resources to achieve safety, quality, cost, and delivery objectives.

* Build effective relationships with customers and suppliers and respond quickly to operational, material, scheduling, or service issues.
* Provide clear reporting on plant financials and key operating indicators, including variances, corrective actions, and improvement results.
* Collaborate with other Metrie teams to share best practices and support broader manufacturing and business priorities.

**Who You Are**

You are a practical and experienced manufacturing leader who enjoys being close to the operation and working alongside the team. You are comfortable in a hands-on manufacturing environment where quality and customer commitments matter and leaders are willing to roll up their sleeves. You set clear expectations, follow through on commitments, and build trust through consistent leadership.

**You bring:**

* A minimum of five years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, with a strong track record of leading, coaching and developing teams.
* Experience driving manufacturing performance across safety, quality, production, cost and customer delivery.

* Excellent communication and relationship-building skills across employees, customers, suppliers, and leadership teams.

**NOTICE: The posting for local applicants only - is not for those applying for a global assignment and/or for employees working outside of Cipla's U.S. Subsidiaries or Affiliates.**

  

**Job Title**: Senior. Manager, Quality Control

**FLSA Classification**: Full-Time, Exempt Professional

**Work Location**: Central Islip, NY (Unit 3)

**Work Hours:** General Shift: 8:30AM – 5:00PM (may vary based on business needs)

**Reports To**: Quality Control Director

**Salary: $103,000 - $136,000**

  

**Position Summary**

The Manager, Finished Product & Stability Quality Control is responsible for leading all analytical testing, stability program execution, laboratory compliance activities, investigations, and personnel management associated with Finished Product and Stability testing. The role ensures compliance with cGMP, FDA, ICH, USP, Data Integrity, and internal quality requirements while supporting product release, stability commitments, regulatory inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Manage Finished Product and Stability testing activities to support commercial product release and ongoing stability programs.
* Oversee testing and review of assay, related substances, chromatographic purity, degradation products, dissolution, content uniformity, residual solvents, and other compendial requirements.
* Ensure timely execution of stability sample pulls, testing, data review, trending, and reporting activities.
* Lead laboratory investigations including OOS, OOT, deviations, atypical results, and CAPA implementation.
* Review and approve analytical data, laboratory records, chromatograms, and technical reports.
* Support method verification, method transfer, process validation, cleaning validation, and troubleshooting activities.
* Ensure inspection readiness and actively support regulatory and customer audits.
* Supervise, train, mentor, and develop laboratory personnel while ensuring efficient workload distribution and resource utilization.
* Partner with QA, Manufacturing, Validation, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and R&D to meet business and compliance objectives.
  

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or related scientific discipline.
* Minimum 5+ years of pharmaceutical Quality Control experience with at least 3-5 years in a supervisory or managerial role.
* Strong experience supporting FDA-regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.

  

**Technical Knowledge & Competencies**

* Hands-on experience in Finished Product and Stability sample testing within a pharmaceutical Quality Control laboratory. Experience with Raw Material testing is preferred.
* Strong knowledge of chromatographic techniques including assay testing, related substances (impurity profiling), degradation product analysis, and chromatographic purity determination using HPLC, UPLC, GC, and IC systems.
* Proficient in operation, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management of analytical instruments including HPLC, UPLC, GC, IC, Dissolution Testers, Karl Fischer, FTIR, UV-Vis, and XRPD.
* Thorough understanding of Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) product testing requirements and regulatory expectations.
* Strong technical expertise in pharmaceutical analytical methodologies, laboratory investigations, data review, and compliance-driven laboratory operations.
* Working knowledge of cGMP, GLP, GDP, Data Integrity requirements, USP, ICH guidelines, and FDA expectations.
* Experience with chromatography data systems and laboratory software including Empower, LabSolutions, Tiamo, and other computerized laboratory systems.
* Working knowledge of Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), Electronic Laboratory Notebook (ELN), and Quality Management Systems such as TrackWise.
* Demonstrated experience in method execution, method troubleshooting, data review, technical assessments, and investigation management.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and customer audits, including USFDA, customer, and corporate audits.
* Strong leadership, communication, documentation, decision-making, and problem-solving skills with the ability to effectively manage teams and collaborate across functions.

  

**GLOBAL COMPANY**

  

Cipla is a leading global pharmaceutical company, dedicated to high-quality, branded and generic medicines. We are trusted by healthcare professionals and patients across geographies. Over the last eight decades, we have strengthened our leadership in India’s pharmaceutical industry and fortified our promise of strengthening our global focus by consolidating and deepening our presence in the key markets of India, South Africa, the U.S., and other economies of the emerging world.

  

Cipla employs handpicked professionals not just for their knowledge and experience but for their zeal to make a difference to the world of healthcare. The company believes that our biggest assets are the employees, who lead us to prosperity and growth in the future. Driven by the vision, none shall be denied, Cipla’s focus has always been on making affordable, world-class medicines with a reputation for uncompromising quality standards across the world.

  

**CIPLA NEW YORK (INVAGEN PHARMACEUTICALS, INC.)**

  

About InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, a Cipla subsidiary InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is engaged in the development, manufacture, marketing, and distribution of generic prescription medicines with focus on a range of therapeutic areas, including cardiovascular, anti-infective, CNS, anti-inflammatory, anti-diabetic, and anti-depressants. The company was founded in 2003 and is based in Central Islip and Hauppauge, New York. As of February 18, 2016, InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Cipla (EU) Limited.

**EEO Statement**

  

Cipla is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, genetic information, disability, or protected veteran status.

Quality Management Systems/Compliance

**This is where** your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.
